repro:P11.title: Reproducible installation and CI — reproduction against current recoup main (e746f46)

subfindings.claim: Test script uses --passWithNoTests, so a future empty/misconfigured suite would exit 0 instead of failing CI.
subfindings.evidence: package.json:11 — "test": "vitest run --passWithNoTests". vitest.config.mts:7 scopes collection to include: ["convex/**/*.test.ts"] only (no src/ frontend test glob exists at all). No .github workflow or any other CI gate rejects a zero-test run; docs/team/VERIFICATION.md:6 and docs/reviews/2026-09-21-production-readiness-baseline.md:20 already flag this same risk ('not acceptance evidence (passWithNoTests)' / 'CI must not allow a future empty suite to pass') and neither doc records it as fixed.
subfindings.repro: grep -n passWithNoTests package.json; cat vitest.config.mts. Currently 31 files / 575 tests are real and pass (`npm test` exit 0), so today's run is not a false pass — but nothing guards against a *future* silent-empty pass, and there is no CI to enforce a minimum test count.

subfindings.claim: Lockfile/generated Convex API consistency is unverified from a clean checkout.
subfindings.evidence: No .github/ directory exists (confirmed) and no CI config of any kind exists outside node_modules. This exact failure mode bit the team before: docs/team/VERIFICATION.md:35 records an isolated worktree where 'typecheck fails only from stale committed `_generated/api.d.ts`', and docs/team/DECISIONS.md D50 codifies the fix as a manual-discipline convention ('Whoever adds or renames a Convex module runs npx convex codegen and includes convex/_generated/api.d.ts in the same commit'), not an enforced check. package-lock.json and convex/_generated/{api.d.ts,api.js,dataModel.d.ts,server.d.ts,server.js} are both git-tracked, so the artifacts exist, but nothing automatically verifies them.
subfindings.repro: Reproduced what CI would do via `git worktree add --detach` at HEAD e746f46 (isolated from the tracked tree; removed afterward, `git status`/`git worktree list` confirmed clean): `npm ci` succeeded, left package-lock.json byte-identical (empty `git diff --stat`), `npm run typecheck` exited 0, and `npm test` reported 'Test Files 31 passed (31) / Tests 575 passed (575)' — matching the stated 575-test baseline. So on this commit the artifacts ARE consistent; the claim is precisely that nothing verifies this automatically on every future commit, which remains true.

subfindings.claim: postinstall runs patch-package, but patch-package is only a devDependency, so behavior under a production install (NODE_ENV=production / --omit=dev) is undefined.
subfindings.evidence: package.json:14 `"postinstall": "patch-package"`; package.json:41 lists `"patch-package": "^8.0.1"` under devDependencies only. The patch it applies, patches/@agentmail+convex+0.1.0.patch, fixes a real production runtime bug per commit 59a9df4 ('performSend threw AGENTMAIL_API_KEY is not set') — production correctness depends on this patch being applied. docs/reviews/2026-09-21-production-readiness-baseline.md:59 already flagged this gap and explicitly noted 'A production-only install was not run during this review' — this reproduction closes that gap.
subfindings.repro: In the same isolated worktree, after `rm -rf node_modules`, ran `npm ci --omit=dev` (production install mode): it does not merely skip the patch silently, the install hard-fails: `sh: patch-package: command not found` / `npm error code 127` / `npm error command failed`. Verified the real npm exit code (not a piped tail's code) was 127. node_modules/.bin/patch-package is absent afterward, so the AgentMail patch is never applied in this mode. This is worse than 'undefined behavior' — it is a deterministic, reproducible hard failure of `npm ci --omit=dev` (equivalently `NODE_ENV=production npm ci`).

subfindings.claim: Dependency audit has not been done.
subfindings.evidence: No file under docs/ mentions 'npm audit', a CVE, or any dependency-vulnerability review. Running `npm audit --omit=dev` in the clean worktree surfaces one CRITICAL advisory already reachable in a production dependency: `@auth/core <=0.41.2` (package.json:19 pins `^0.41.1`, package-lock.json resolves 0.41.1) — GHSA-7rqj-j65f-68wh (email-normalizer homoglyph '@' bypass), GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj (uncaught exception on malformed Bearer header), GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279 (OAuth state/nonce/PKCE cookies not bound to provider). This is pulled in transitively by @convex-dev/auth, which convex/auth.ts registers with the Password provider only (per the existing baseline review), so the OAuth-state/PKCE advisory is likely not reachable in this app, but the email-normalizer bypass is worth checking against the actual sign-in/sign-up email-matching code — that triage has not been done anywhere in the repo.
subfindings.repro: cd <clean checkout>; npm ci; npm audit --omit=dev → '1 critical severity vulnerability' naming @auth/core. No prior audit output, triage, or accepted-risk note exists in git history or docs for this package.

subfindings.claim: (Instruction-mandated check) whether any P11 claim is a race/fault-window bug convex-test could exercise.
subfindings.evidence: None of the four P11 claims are runtime concurrency/fault-window bugs inside Convex functions — they are install-tooling and CI-process gaps (npm script flags, lockfile/codegen drift, postinstall dependency placement, dependency-audit hygiene). Per convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md's Testing guidelines (read before touching Convex code), convex-test runs mutations against an edge-runtime harness and serializes each `t.mutation(...)` call to completion — it has no concept of `npm ci`, postinstall scripts, package-lock.json, or `npm audit`, and cannot spawn or fault-inject an install process.
subfindings.repro: What would actually demonstrate this class of gap is a CI job that: (a) checks out clean and runs `npm ci` twice / re-runs `npx convex codegen` and diffs for drift, (b) separately runs `npm ci --omit=dev` and asserts the expected (non-crashing, or explicitly-documented-crashing) outcome, and (c) runs `npm audit --omit=dev` against an allowlist. None exists. I reproduced the equivalent manually via a throwaway `git worktree add --detach` under /private/tmp (removed afterward with `git worktree remove --force`; main repo verified clean via `git status`), not via convex-test, since convex-test is the wrong tool for this class of claim.

existing_tests: None. Grepped all 31 files under convex/**/*.test.ts (budget, claims, drafts, examples, followUps, inbound, insights, intake, lib/ai, lib/errors, lib/imageUrl, lib/ledger, lib/money, lib/offerMatch, lib/passage, lib/policyText, lib/priceStatsClient, lib/schemas, lib/shopsavvy, lib/verdict, lib/watchUrl, notify, offers, policies, priceWatch, profiles, purchases, replies, test.setup, tracking, watches) for patch-package, postinstall, passWithNoTests, package-lock, 'npm audit', 'npm ci' — zero matches. Expected: convex-test exercises Convex function logic, not the npm install/CI pipeline, so nothing in the 575-test suite covers any P11 claim.
repro:P11.notes:
Reproduced entirely against /Users/nihalnihalani/Desktop/Github/recoup at HEAD e746f46 (main, clean) without modifying the tracked working tree: used `git worktree add --detach` into /private/tmp/p11_repro (plus two copies for the dev-vs-production install comparison) instead of touching the repo directly; never ran `npx convex dev`, codegen, or anything deployment-facing; all throwaway worktrees were removed with `git worktree remove --force` and the primary repo verified clean (`git status`, `git worktree list`) afterward. Read convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md before touching any Convex code, per instructions.

Headline result: three of the four claims are still_present and now backed by direct reproduction rather than inference — most notably, production-mode install (`npm ci --omit=dev`) does not merely have "undefined" patch behavior as the backlog item states, it hard-fails with real exit code 127 because the patch-package binary is absent (it's devDependencies-only), and this also means the AgentMail runtime-crash patch (which fixes a real production bug per commit 59a9df4) would silently never be applied in that install mode. The dependency-audit claim is confirmed with a concrete, currently-unreviewed critical CVE (@auth/core <=0.41.2). The lockfile/generated-API claim is nuanced: on the current commit everything IS empirically consistent (clean-room npm ci + typecheck + the full 575-test run all pass, matching the stated baseline exactly), but the underlying claim — that nothing automatically verifies this on every future commit, because there is no CI — remains true. The --passWithNoTests claim is a literal, unchanged fact in package.json:11. None of the four claims is a runtime race/fault-window bug, so convex-test is not the right tool for any of them; I documented precisely why and what tooling (a real CI job) would be needed instead. No fixes were applied, per instructions, beyond noting a one-sentence direction inside each claim's evidence.

repro:P01.title: Email identity, consent, and recovery — reproduction against current main (575 tests)

subfindings.claim: No email verification before automatic alert delivery
subfindings.evidence: convex/auth.ts:1-5 calls `Password` with no config object at all (`providers: [Password]`), so `config.verify` is undefined. In node_modules/@convex-dev/auth/src/providers/Password.ts:229 the sign-in code only checks `if (config.verify && !account.emailVerified)`, which is unconditionally skipped, so `users.emailVerificationTime` (schema field defined in node_modules/@convex-dev/auth/dist/server/implementation/types.js:33) is never populated for any account. On the send side, convex/notify.ts's `dropContext` (lines 194-242) computes `to` from `user?.email?.trim()` (line 206) and never reads or checks `emailVerificationTime`; `claimDrop` (lines 131-170) likewise never checks it before scheduling `internal.notify.sendDrop`.
subfindings.repro: Wrote a throwaway convex-test (deleted after running) at /private/tmp/notify-repro/verification_repro.test.ts with a temp vitest config. It inserts a user via the existing `signedIn` test helper, patches in an email while leaving `emailVerificationTime` undefined (mirroring what the real Password provider actually produces), creates an active watch, and calls `internal.watches.recordWatchCheck` twice to produce a qualifying price drop. After flushing the scheduler, the resulting `mailLog` row reached `status: "sent"` with `agentmail.sendMessage` actually invoked with `to: "unverified@stranger.example"`. Test passed (1/1), confirming nothing in the send path gates on verification. Files created/removed: /private/tmp/notify-repro/verification_repro.test.ts, /private/tmp/notify-repro/vitest.config.repro.mts, and a temporary /Users/nihalnihalani/Desktop/Github/recoup/vitest.config.repro.mts (all deleted; `git status` on the repo is clean).

subfindings.claim: No password recovery
subfindings.evidence: convex/auth.ts:1-5 passes no `reset` option to `Password`. node_modules/@convex-dev/auth/src/providers/Password.ts:166-169 throws `Password reset is not enabled for password` whenever the `"reset"` flow is attempted and `config.reset` is undefined (same for `"reset-verification"` at lines 179-181). `grep -rn "reset" convex/*.ts` (excluding _generated) turns up nothing resembling a reset/OTP email provider, and src/pages/SignIn.tsx's `Flow` type is restricted to `"signIn" | "signUp"` (line 5) with no reset UI at all.
subfindings.repro: Not a race/fault window — a static configuration absence, directly shown by reading the Password provider source cited above; calling `signIn("password", { flow: "reset", email })` from this app's convexAuth config throws immediately inside the library. No convex-test needed; a throwaway test would just re-assert the library throws, which the source already proves.

subfindings.claim: Verification/preference not rechecked at send time
subfindings.evidence: convex/notify.ts's `dropContext` (lines 194-242) does freshly re-read `watch.status` (line 214) and `user.email` (line 206) at send time — but there is no verification field or preference field anywhere in the schema for it to recheck (see next two findings). So the underlying gap isn't a stale recheck, it's that neither claim time (`claimDrop`, lines 131-170) nor send time (`dropContext`/`sendDrop`) ever consult `emailVerificationTime` or any opt-out flag, because none is read at either point.
subfindings.repro: Same throwaway test as the first finding demonstrates this directly: the send succeeds regardless of verification state at both claim and send time.

subfindings.claim: No opt-out/unsubscribe
subfindings.evidence: convex/schema.ts's `profiles` table (lines 39-40) has only `userId`, `inboxId`, `inboxEmail`; authTables' `users` (node_modules/@convex-dev/auth/dist/server/implementation/types.js:26-38) has `name/image/email/emailVerificationTime/phone/phoneVerificationTime/isAnonymous` — no preference or opt-out field. The alert email body built in convex/notify.ts lines 224-237 contains no unsubscribe link or opt-out instruction (it explicitly documents omitting even the app link when it would be a localhost URL, but never mentions opting out). `grep -rn "unsubscribe\|optOut\|opt-out" convex/ src/` returns no matches anywhere in the app.
subfindings.repro: Static absence — nothing to invoke with a test; there is no field or mutation to exercise.

subfindings.claim: Suppressed emails not preserved as in-app drops with reason
subfindings.evidence: convex/notify.ts `claimDrop` (lines 151-167) always inserts a `mailLog` row and sets `status: "failed"`, `error: limitError` when the daily/global cap is hit. `dropContext` (lines 212-216) computes a human-readable `problem` string when the row can't be mailed (watch gone, watch inactive, no email, no inbox), and `sendDrop`'s handler (line 337) routes that into `finishDrop` (lines 245-260), which patches `status: "failed"`, `error`. The `drops` query (lines 423-455) surfaces `status` and `error` per row, and the UI renders it (src/pages/Watching.tsx's `Drops()` component, ~lines 103-140, shows a `Chip` with `drop.error ?? "Not emailed"` when status is `failed`). Covered by convex/notify.test.ts describe block "a drop that cannot be mailed is still recorded" (lines 261-333), including "no account email: failed row with the reason, no throw, nothing sent" (line 262), "no inbox of any kind: failed row with the reason" (line 294), and the daily/global cap describe block (lines 406-479).
subfindings.repro: Not needed — existing test suite already exercises this path and passes as part of the 575-test baseline.

subfindings.claim: Changing address does not invalidate verification
subfindings.evidence: No mutation anywhere in convex/*.ts patches `users.email` after account creation outside of test helpers (`grep -rn "db.patch(user\|patch(userId" convex/*.ts` and a broader `\.email\b` grep show only reads in drafts.ts/notify.ts/profiles.ts). No page or component in src/pages or src/components exposes an email-change form — the only `type="email"` inputs in the app are SignIn.tsx's sign-up/sign-in fields (src/pages/SignIn.tsx:126) and an unrelated merchant-contact-email field in src/components/purchase/RuleCard.tsx:274. The only writer of `users.email` is the Password provider's own account-creation code, invoked once at sign-up.
subfindings.repro: No feature exists to exercise: there is no in-app "change my email" mutation or UI to write a test against. Combined with finding 1 (verification is never turned on for anyone in the first place, since `config.verify` is unset), the specific invalidation-on-change concern has no live code path in the current app to reproduce for or against.

subfindings.claim: UI copy does not distinguish per-message merchant approval from automatic alerts
subfindings.evidence: src/pages/SignIn.tsx line 19 shows every signed-out visitor the unqualified promise: "You approve every message before it is sent. Recoup never files claims in bulk." That gate is `drafts.approveAndSend` (convex/drafts.ts:374, a `mutation` requiring an explicit user call from the "Approve & send" button in src/components/claim/Composer.tsx:377) and it applies only to merchant-facing claim mail. convex/notify.ts's own module header states this directly: "This path never goes through `drafts.approveAndSend` itself: that gate is for mail to merchants, and this mail only ever goes to `users.email`" (convex/notify.ts lines 17-19). Price-drop alerts are instead scheduled fully automatically from `watches.recordWatchCheck` -> `claimDrop` (notify.ts:131-170) -> `sendDrop` (notify.ts:304-344) with zero per-message user action. `grep -rn "approve\|before it is sent" src/**/*.tsx` finds no qualifying text anywhere that carves automatic alerts out of the SignIn.tsx promise.
subfindings.repro: Textual/copy issue, not a logic race — no test needed and none exists (this is UI copy, not covered by any test file).

existing_tests: convex/notify.test.ts — describe('claiming a drop inside recordWatchCheck'), describe('a drop that cannot be mailed is still recorded') [lines 261-333: no-email and no-inbox produce failed rows with reasons], describe('daily cap') [lines 406-479: per-user and global caps recorded as failed rows], describe('F3: claimed -> queued -> sent'), describe('notify.applyDropOutcome (F3)'), describe('notify.drops'), describe('publicAppUrl') — none of these touch emailVerificationTime, password reset, or opt-out, and the `account()` test helper (notify.test.ts:39-52) never sets emailVerificationTime.
convex/watches.test.ts — exercises recordWatchCheck's wiring into claimDrop but not the auth/verification layer.

convex/test.setup.ts — the shared `signedIn` helper (lines 32-35) inserts a `users` row directly via `ctx.db.insert`, bypassing the actual Password provider entirely, so no test in the 575-test suite exercises real sign-up/sign-in/reset/verify flows.
No convex/auth.test.ts (or equivalent) exists at all — grep of convex/ for an auth-specific test file found none.
repro:P01.notes: Baseline claims of 'several historic findings already fixed' checks out for exactly one of the seven concrete claims here (the suppressed-email/in-app-drop backstop, via F1-era claim-before-send + F3-era claimed/queued/sent work already landed in notify.ts). The other five substantive claims (verification gate, password recovery, recheck-at-send, opt-out, and the misleading 'approve every message' copy) are still present and are structural/configuration gaps, not races — convex/auth.ts is 5 lines using bare Password with neither verify nor reset configured, and there is no schema field, mutation, or UI for email preferences or email change at all. The 'changing address does not invalidate verification' claim could not be reproduced because there is no email-change feature in the current codebase to test in the first place. All repro artifacts (throwaway test file, two temp vitest configs — one briefly placed in the repo root to work around ESM module resolution for vitest/config when the config lives outside the workspace, one in /private/tmp) were deleted after the single test run; git status on the repo confirmed no residue.

repro:P12.notes: Current HEAD is e521de9 on main; `npx vitest run` reproduces 575/575 passing across 31 files, matching docs/team/DECISIONS.md:87 (D61)'s stated baseline, so the code under review matches what the backlog item was written against. None of the 7 claims are a race or concurrency fault window in the convex-test sense (no two mutations contending on the same document), so no throwaway concurrency test was needed or attempted; where a claim was about an observable code behavior (the redaction gap), an already-existing test in the suite (offers.test.ts:182-206) was sufficient to demonstrate the raw, unredacted, uncorrelated error reaching the log line, so no new throwaway test file was created. subfindings.claim: Missing docs for SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY, ALERTS_INBOX_ID, and APP_URL.
subfindings.evidence: README.md's env-var table (lines 54-60) lists only OPENAI_API_KEY, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, AGENTMAIL_API_KEY, AGENTMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and the auth trio. subfindings.claim: Missing docs for AI model selection and webhook/signing setup.
subfindings.evidence: AI model: actually documented — hackathon.md:56 names the model ('gpt-5.6-terra', convex/lib/ai.ts:6) and explains the money-safety guarantee around model output (hackathon.md:62). Not mentioned in README.md's config sections, so a README-only reader still misses it, but the documentation exists in the repo. Webhook/signing setup: README.md:64 tells an operator to create an AgentMail webhook at /agentmail/webhook and set AGENTMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and README.md:62 states the route rejects events until the secret is set — enough to get it working, but nothing documents the signature header/algorithm, secret rotation, or bad-signature behavior; convex/http.ts:11-26 delegates verification entirely into the opaque agentmail.handleWebhook component.
subfindings.repro: grep -n model/gpt across README.md and hackathon.md; read convex/http.ts:1-29 (webhook route has zero inline documentation of what handleWebhook checks).

subfindings.claim: No correlation IDs, and operational-signal redaction is real but narrow (covers only inbound/intake extraction failures shown to end users; every other failure category logs raw, uncorrelated errors).
subfindings.evidence: A genuine, unit-tested redaction function exists: convex/lib/errors.ts:16 sanitizeError, used at convex/intake.ts:126,160 and convex/inbound.ts:185 (D58) to turn a raw caught error into one of 4 safe buckets for processedEvents.errorSummary (the only thing the board's 'needs attention' list shows a user); raw lastError is kept server-side. Tested in convex/lib/errors.test.ts (4 cases). But: (1) it's a user-facing redaction, not an operator-facing structured/redacted log; (2) no correlation ID exists anywhere — grep for correlationId|traceId|requestId|reqId across convex/ and src/ returns zero hits, so nothing ties a webhook receipt to its downstream processing, price-check, notification, or send-callback outcome; (3) every other failure category logs the raw err object with no sanitization and no id: convex/notify.ts:326,340 (notification), convex/priceWatch.ts:373 and convex/watches.ts:604 (price checks), convex/offers.ts:482,494,500,667 (offers/market search), convex/policies.ts:186 (policy fetch); (4) budget exhaustion (convex/lib/budget.ts consumeBudget/consumeGlobalBudget) throws a ConvexError with zero console/log signal at all; (5) send-callback outcomes (convex/drafts.ts:527 sendError: (status.errorMessage ?? ...).slice(...)) write the raw provider error text into a user-visible claim field, unredacted, with no operator-side signal; (6) scheduler backlog has no signal — convex/watches.ts:739-763 sweep silently caps at WATCH_SWEEP_PAGE with no log/metric when more watches are due than the page can take.
subfindings.repro: Demonstrated by an existing test, no new throwaway needed: convex/offers.test.ts:182-206 ('stores nothing and does not throw when the search or a page fails') makes OfferDeps.search throw Error("402 insufficient credits"), spies on console.error, and asserts only toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2) — the raw, unredacted, uncorrelated message is what actually reaches the spy; the test never inspects or redacts it. subfindings.claim: Archive churn hides active data — userWatches takes 40 newest before archived filtering; userPurchases takes 40 newest before active filtering
subfindings.evidence: convex/insights.ts:86-92 `userWatches()` does `.query("watches").withIndex("by_user", userId).order("desc").take(MAX_WATCHES=40)` with NO status predicate; every caller (activity() L112-113, sources() L304-305) filters `status === "archived"` only AFTER the take(40). Same pattern for purchases at L94-101: `userPurchases()` takes 40 newest by `by_user` (sorted by _creationTime, status-agnostic) then does `.filter(p => p.status === "active")` in memory. The `by_user` index on both tables is single-field (schema.ts:48 purchases, :92 watches), so ordering is purely by creation time, not by status — archiving a row does not move it out of the newest-N window. Nothing bounds total (incl. archived) row count: watches.ts's `consumeCreateLimit` (L309-331) only counts LIVE_STATUSES (active/paused/bought) against MAX_WATCHES_PER_USER=50; archived rows are never counted toward any cap, so an account's archived-watch total grows unboundedly over time with normal archive/re-add usage.

subfindings.claim: Double counting — a watch marked bought increments both the bought-watch tally and the purchase item created from it
subfindings.evidence: convex/insights.ts:304-308: for each live (non-archived) watch, `if (watch.status === "bought") target.bought += 1;` keyed on `watch.merchantDomain` (L306). Separately, L335-343: for each active, non-example purchase, every item in it adds `target.bought += 1;` keyed on `purchase.merchantDomain` (L337). `watches.ts:markBought` (L480-565) creates exactly this pairing: it inserts a purchase with `merchantDomain: watch.merchantDomain` (L519) and exactly one item (L525-534), then `ctx.db.patch(watch._id, { status: "bought", purchaseId })` (L561) — the watch row is never archived or removed. Because the domains are identical by construction, both loops add to the same `SourceRow`, so one bought item is counted twice in `sources().bought`.

subfindings.claim: Money summed/compared across currencies
subfindings.evidence: convex/insights.ts's `tally()` (L282-302) and the offers loop (L316-332) update `target.bestCents` by pure numeric comparison of `observedCents`/`lastCents` (L294, L298, L327) with no currency check, and set `target.currency = target.currency ?? check.currency` (L296) / `store.currency = store.currency ?? offer.currency` (L330) — a nullish-coalescing assignment that only fires once per row and then never updates again, even when a later, cheaper observation in a different currency becomes the new `bestCents`. Practically this triggers whenever one store domain aggregates watches/purchases in more than one currency. Caveat: this is a comparison/mislabeling bug, not a literal `+=` sum of mismatched currencies — nothing in insights.ts adds monetary amounts together across rows; bestCents is a min, not a sum. Also note bestCents/bestSubject are currently unused by the frontend (src/components/dashboard/SourcesCard.tsx renders watching/bought/offers/drops/checks/priced only; grep for bestCents/bestSubject in src/ returns nothing), so today's user-visible blast radius is nil even though the query-layer bug is real.

subfindings.claim: recordSnapshot sets marketFetchedAt even when the key is missing or the provider fails, and market.refresh refuses any watch with that stamp (i.e. failures are permanently terminal, not recoverable once ShopSavvy is configured or the outage clears)
subfindings.evidence: convex/market.ts:106-121 recordSnapshot unconditionally does `await ctx.db.patch(watchId, { marketFetchedAt: now, marketNote: note })` regardless of outcome. convex/market.ts:169-191 lookup: on missing key (fetchSnapshot returns null, market.ts:49-51) note='Market history is not configured on this deployment'; on a thrown error (market.ts:182-186) note=the cleaned error message; both branches still call recordSnapshot with points:[] which stamps marketFetchedAt the same as a real success. convex/market.ts:258-272 refresh throws ConvexError('Market history has already been looked up for this item') whenever `watch.marketFetchedAt !== undefined` (line 265), with no branch that re-checks marketNote or distinguishes why it was set. subfindings.claim: No not_configured/queued/running/success/empty/retryable/terminal state distinction
subfindings.evidence: convex/schema.ts:89 the only persisted state is `marketFetchedAt: v.optional(v.number())` plus `marketNote: v.optional(v.string())` — a timestamp-or-not plus a free-text note, not a discriminated/enum status. There is no 'queued'/'running' state at all: between a mutation scheduling internal.market.lookup (market.ts:269, watches.ts:721) and that action actually executing, marketFetchedAt is still undefined, indistinguishable from 'never asked'. not-configured, provider-error, and empty-result produce different note *text* (market.ts:181,183-185,237) but all set marketFetchedAt identically and are treated identically by every reader: watches.ts:220-243 summarise() only branches on marketPoints.length===0 vs not and marketNote===undefined vs not — never on which kind of note it is — and market.refresh (market.ts:265-267) blocks on marketFetchedAt alone, never on note content.

subfindings.claim: No transactional claim before the paid lookup, so simultaneous manual refresh and automatic checks can duplicate provider calls
subfindings.evidence: The only 'claim' anywhere is the read-check `watch.marketFetchedAt === undefined` performed independently in three places that never themselves write marketFetchedAt: market.watchForMarket (market.ts:69-85, called from the lookup action), market.refresh (market.ts:258-272), and the automatic path inside watches.recordWatchCheck (watches.ts:719-722, additionally gated by a global-budget tryConsumeGlobalBudget). None of these mutations patches marketFetchedAt; the only write happens later, inside market.recordSnapshot (market.ts:109-162), which runs in a *separately scheduled* action (market.lookup, market.ts:169-241) invoked via `ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, ...)`. Because the claim (the patch) is decoupled from the check by an async scheduler hop plus, on the real path, a live HTTP call to ShopSavvy (market.ts:58-66, up to TIMEOUT_MS=30s), any second caller that reads the watch before that action finishes also passes the check and schedules its own lookup.
subfindings.repro: Wrote and ran a throwaway convex-test (under /private/tmp, deleted after): (1) called api.market.refresh for a watch — schedules lookup job #1 and does NOT set marketFetchedAt (verified still undefined right after); (2) called internal.watches.recordWatchCheck with an accepted price, which re-read the same watch, still saw marketFetchedAt===undefined, and scheduled a SECOND market:lookup job — confirmed via ctx.db.system.query('_scheduled_functions'): two pending 'market:lookup' jobs for the same watchId, marketFetchedAt still undefined at that point. Then set SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY, stubbed global fetch with vi.fn() returning a valid ShopSavvy envelope, and ran t.finishAllScheduledFunctions(vi.runAllTimers): the fetch spy was called exactly 2 times — two real provider calls for one watch, before either action's recordSnapshot claimed it; marketFetchedAt only became defined afterward. This needed no true concurrency, and convex-test's mutation serialization does not prevent it, because the two mutations never conflict on writing marketFetchedAt at all — they only conflict on the later, decoupled write inside recordSnapshot. The one variant convex-test genuinely cannot show is two requests racing inside Convex's OCC layer on the exact same in-flight transaction (it runs mutations to completion one at a time rather than interleaving true concurrent transactions); that would need a live deployment or a harness that can pause a mutation mid-commit. It is not needed here: the sequential-with-async-gap reproduction above already demonstrates the identical root cause (check and claim live in different, arbitrarily-separated transactions) and is arguably the more realistic real-world trigger (an accepted check schedules the automatic lookup, then before that job runs the user clicks Refresh).

subfindings.claim: No capped retry/backoff
subfindings.evidence: market.lookup (market.ts:169-241) never lets fetchSnapshot's errors propagate — it catches them (market.ts:182-186) and turns them into a note, so the action always 'succeeds' from the scheduler's point of view and there is nothing for a platform-level retry to trigger even if one were configured. repro:P04.title: Historical-price quality and product matching (ShopSavvy / market.ts / offer matching / verdict)

subfindings.claim: Median outlier filtering does not prove variant/condition/bundle/shipping/currency match
subfindings.evidence: convex/lib/shopsavvy.ts:157-166 `withoutOutliers` is a pure price-band heuristic (median*0.4..median*1.75) with no field of the offer other than `cents` consulted. `condition` is parsed at shopsavvy.ts:128 but grepping the whole convex/ tree shows it is never read anywhere else — a `used`/`refurbished` listing is treated identically to `new`. `flattenHistory` (shopsavvy.ts:168-189), which builds the points later shown on the chart and fed to `verdict()`, does not check `availability` either (only `marketStats`'s single 'best' computation does, at shopsavvy.ts:215) — an out-of-stock listing's price still becomes a kept history point. There is no bundle/shipping-inclusion signal in the ShopSavvy envelope at all, so nothing exists to check.
subfindings.repro: convex/lib/shopsavvy.test.ts already documents the same limitation is understood ('drops an accessory and a bundle but keeps a real sale' — a *price-band* heuristic, not identity proof) but no test exercises `condition` or `availability` filtering because the code never looks at those fields. No new test needed beyond reading the source: `grep -n "\.condition\b" convex --include="*.ts"` returns only the one parse site.

subfindings.claim: Unknown currency handling is undefined
subfindings.evidence: convex/lib/shopsavvy.ts:178 `if ((point.currency ?? currency) !== currency) continue;` and shopsavvy.ts:213 `if ((offer.currency ?? currency) !== currency) continue;` both use `?? currency` (the TARGET/watch currency) as the fallback when a point/offer has no currency at all. A point/offer with `currency: null` therefore always passes the equality check and is silently treated as if it were already confirmed to be in the watch's currency, rather than being excluded or flagged as unknown.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway test (run and deleted): an offer with no `currency` field at all and `price: 1` beat a real `currency:"USD", price:500` offer for `marketStats(...).best` — `flattenHistory` also kept the no-currency point as a `USD` history point. Command used: `npx vitest run --config vitest.p04.temp.mts` against `/private/tmp/p04-repro/shopsavvy_gaps.test.ts` (both assertions passed, confirming the bug). Existing coverage in convex/lib/shopsavvy.test.ts only tests a *declared* mismatched currency (`currency: "EUR"` vs `"USD"`, correctly rejected) — the null/undefined-currency case is untested.

subfindings.claim: Stale-listing handling is undefined
subfindings.evidence: No staleness threshold exists anywhere in convex/lib/shopsavvy.ts or convex/market.ts — an offer's own `observedAt` (which the code's own doc comment at shopsavvy.ts:56 admits can be years old: 'Old timestamps are common and are shown as read') is used unfiltered in `flattenHistory`/`marketStats`, and is copied as-is into `offers.lastCheckedAt` at convex/market.ts:229/155 when a ShopSavvy store becomes a candidate row. There is no code path that rejects, discounts, or separately labels an old point; the only mitigation is that the true timestamp is preserved and rendered honestly (`src/components/watching/StoreCompare.tsx:89` shows `Read {ago(now, row.checkedAt)}`, and `MarketHistory.tsx` shows `since {day(market.since)}`), so a stale listing is not hidden, just not specially guarded against.
subfindings.repro: Not separately reproduced beyond the source read above; this is a design gap (no threshold), not a crash/race. The 'confirmed candidate' path is the concrete exposure: a user can `offers.confirm` a ShopSavvy-sourced candidate carrying a years-old price with no warning beyond the generic note 'Listed by ShopSavvy; confirm it is the same item' (convex/market.ts:156), after which it competes for `best` in convex/offers.ts:368-378 on equal footing with a freshly-scraped price.

subfindings.claim: Historical provider data could independently create claims or alerts
subfindings.evidence: Traced every call site: `openClaim` is called only from convex/examples.ts:115,198 (seed/demo data), convex/claims.ts:144 (user-initiated return_credit), convex/intake.ts:491, and convex/priceWatch.ts:293 (D20 price-adjustment claim, gated on `args.observedCents` from the item's OWN scrape in `recordCheck`). Nothing in convex/market.ts or convex/watches.ts's market-lookup branch calls `openClaim`. Alerts: `claimDrop` (convex/notify.ts:126) is called only once, at convex/watches.ts:713, with `observedCents` sourced from `recordWatchCheck`'s own `args` (the watch's own page scrape), never from `marketPrices`/ShopSavvy. The architectural boundary described in the shopsavvy.ts/market.ts header comments ('It never opens a claim and never sends an alert') holds for the current code.
subfindings.repro: Static trace via grep of every `openClaim(` and `internal.notify.sendDrop`/`claimDrop(` call site in convex/ (excluding tests); none touch `marketPrices`, `watch.marketFetchedAt`, or `offers.source === "shopsavvy"`.

subfindings.claim: Confirmed offer matching may silently authorize later variants
subfindings.evidence: Two real guards exist and are exercised: (1) convex/offers.ts:551-556 `recordCandidates` only refreshes a `confirmed` row's price when the NEW candidate's `productUrl` is byte-identical to the confirmed one (`if (existing.productUrl !== c.productUrl) continue;`) — a different URL at the same store never overwrites a confirmed offer's price. (2) convex/offers.ts:698-699 `recordRechecks` re-decides at write time (`offer.status !== "confirmed"` -> skip), so a user's `reject` landing before an in-flight recheck's result is respected, not silently overridden. (3) `priceFields`/`rejectionReason` (offers.ts:183-200, priceWatch.ts:313-341) reject and clear `lastCents` when a recheck reports `variantMatch !== "exact"`, so an 'unsure'/'none' re-read cannot silently keep asserting a price — this is existing, tested behavior (convex/offers.test.ts:238-244). What is NOT guarded: identity is entirely delegated to the LLM's `variantMatch` judgment against the SAME requested URL — there is no secondary identity signal (canonical/final URL after a store-side redirect, SKU/GTIN, page-title diff) once a URL is confirmed. If a store repoints a confirmed product URL at a successor/similar-named model and the extractor still reports `variantMatch: "exact"` against `watch.name`, the system has no independent check to catch it — that residual risk is inherent to relying solely on model output, not a specific missed code guard.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway convex-test (run and deleted) confirmed guard #2: created a `confirmed` offer, called `api.offers.reject`, then fed `internal.offers.recordRechecks` a fresh (different-price) observation for that same offerId — result: `written === 0`, offer stayed `status: "rejected"` with its original `lastCents: 18000` untouched (not overwritten by the in-flight recheck's `5000`). This demonstrates convex-test CAN show this fault window directly (it is not a true concurrency race in the DB sense — both writes are separate serialized mutations, and the test simply orders them the way a real race would land: reject-then-late-recheck-result). A true simultaneous-mutation race cannot be shown with convex-test since it serializes mutations one at a time; what would show it is a live/staging fault-injection test (delay the scrape, fire `reject` and let the scheduled `recheck` land mid-scrape) — out of scope here per the read-only/no-deploy constraint.

subfindings.claim: Provider envelopes/size/minor units/timestamps/URLs not validated at the boundary
subfindings.evidence: Mixed by sub-claim. Envelope shape: convex/lib/shopsavvy.ts:102-107 `parseSnapshot` does check `typeof body === object`, array/object `data`, and drops the whole snapshot on a malformed root — adequate. Minor units: `toCents` (shopsavvy.ts:21-25) validates finite, positive, safe-integer cents — adequate. URLs on the LIVE write path: convex/market.ts:221 `cleanStoreUrl(offer.productUrl)` routes every store URL through `parseProductUrl` (convex/lib/watchUrl.ts:23-41, which rejects non-http(s), credentials, unusual ports, private/internal hostnames) before it is ever written to `offers` — adequate for the reachable path. Size: NOT bounded — `parseSnapshot`'s `rawOffers` loop (shopsavvy.ts:110-132) and `parsePoints`'s loop (shopsavvy.ts:83-96) iterate the full parsed arrays with no cap; `MARKET_MAX_POINTS`/`MARKET_MAX_STORES` (convex/limits.ts:128,130) are only applied later, in convex/market.ts's `recordSnapshot`/`lookup` (`.slice(0, MARKET_MAX_POINTS)` etc.), i.e. after the full O(n) parse+sort+outlier work already ran inside the action. Timestamps: `epoch()` (shopsavvy.ts:31-36) only checks `Number.isFinite`, with no sanity bound (no rejection of a future or absurdly old date) — this is the root cause that lets a corrupted point reach `verdict.ts`'s unfiltered `market` fallback (see below). Also worth flagging: the exported `marketStats()` function (shopsavvy.ts:202-234, re-exported at market.ts:274) builds `best.productUrl` straight from the RAW parsed `offer.productUrl` with no `cleanStoreUrl`/`parseProductUrl` pass — but this function has no live caller (only `internal.market.lookup` is called from convex/watches.ts:721; nothing calls `marketStats` outside convex/lib/shopsavvy.test.ts), so it is currently dead code, not a reachable defect.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway tests (run and deleted): (a) `parseSnapshot` given 50,000 synthetic offers each with 50 history rows processed all of them with `snap.offers` returning length 50,000 (no cap) — confirms the size gap. (b) verdict.ts repro below confirms the timestamp gap is live-reachable, not just theoretical.

subfindings.claim: (Consequence of the timestamp gap above) verdict()'s market fallback does not filter future/corrupted timestamps the way the watch's own history does
subfindings.evidence: convex/lib/verdict.ts:127-128 filters the watch's OWN `history` with `h.observedAt <= now`; convex/lib/verdict.ts:151 passes `input.market` into `fromMarket()` with no equivalent filter, and `fromMarket` (verdict.ts:86-118) sorts/min/max's the raw array as-is. This is live-reachable: `market` originates from convex/market.ts's `lookup` action (`flattenHistory(...).slice(-MARKET_MAX_POINTS)`, no date-sanity filter), is stored in `marketPrices`, read back by convex/watches.ts:161-166 `marketFor`, and passed unfiltered into `verdict()` at convex/watches.ts:188 inside the public `watches.list`/`watches.get` queries. convex/lib/verdict.test.ts:173 explicitly tests 'ignores observations dated in the future' for the OWN-history path but there is zero mention of `market` anywhere in that test file — confirming the asymmetry is untested, not an intentional documented design choice.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway test (run and deleted): fed `verdict()` a `market` array containing a point dated 2031 (after the supplied `now` of 2026-09-21) at an absurd $1.00, alongside two legitimate ~$50 points, with `history: []` (forcing the market fallback). Result reason string was `'$48.00 is in the usual range ShopSavvy has recorded since Jan 1, 2025 ($1.00 to $52.00).'` — the $1.00 figure, sourced entirely from the impossible future-dated point, is quoted straight to the user as real recorded evidence. Feeding the IDENTICAL bogus point through `history` instead of `market` (same `verdict()` call) produced `'not_enough_history'` and the reason did NOT contain `$1.00` — proving the own-history guard works and the market path lacks it.

subfindings.claim: Missing ShopSavvy credentials must not break core watching
subfindings.evidence: convex/market.ts:49-51 `fetchSnapshot` returns `null` immediately (no throw) when `process.env.SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY` is unset. `lookup` (market.ts:169-186) treats a `null` snapshot as a normal outcome (`note = "Market history is not configured on this deployment"`) and always completes by calling `recordSnapshot`, never throwing past itself. Critically, `lookup` is only ever invoked via `ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.market.lookup, ...)` from convex/watches.ts:721 — fire-and-forget from inside `recordWatchCheck`'s own mutation, which has already committed its own price-check writes (including any drop alert) before scheduling this. Even if `lookup` did throw, it runs as an independent scheduled action and cannot roll back or block the watch-check mutation that scheduled it. Core watching (price checks, verdicts, drop alerts) has no dependency on ShopSavvy being configured.
subfindings.repro: Static trace of `fetchSnapshot`/`lookup`/the scheduling call site; no test needed to demonstrate the absence of a throw path, but convex/priceWatch.test.ts and convex/watches.test.ts already implicitly exercise the watch-check flow without ever setting `SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY` in convex/test.setup.ts, and none of those 575 existing tests fail — corroborating this.

subfindings.claim: (Related, not in the harness's 7-item list, but directly relevant to the same market.ts boundary and matches a defect the baseline report already flagged) recordSnapshot permanently stamps marketFetchedAt even on a config-absent/failed lookup, permanently blocking market.refresh once fixed
subfindings.evidence: convex/market.ts:78 `watchForMarket` returns null (skips the lookup) once `watch.marketFetchedAt !== undefined`; convex/market.ts:121 `recordSnapshot` unconditionally sets `marketFetchedAt: now` on every call, including the missing-key/error branch at market.ts:188-191. convex/market.ts:265-267 `refresh` throws `ConvexError("Market history has already been looked up for this item")` whenever `marketFetchedAt !== undefined`. Net effect: a watch that had its automatic lookup run before `SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY` was configured (or during a transient provider failure) can never be refreshed through the public API again, even after the key is later added — this exactly matches docs/team/DECISIONS.md's D60 note ('market.lookup stamps marketFetchedAt even when SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY is unset, so market.refresh is refused forever once the key is added') and docs/reviews/2026-09-21-production-readiness-baseline.md's 'Confirmed recovery defect' section — both dated today, and the code still matches that description.
subfindings.repro: Static trace only (no new test written): watchForMarket/recordSnapshot/refresh code paths cited above. A convex-test demonstrating this is straightforward (call `internal.market.lookup` with no `SHOPSAVVY_API_KEY` set, then call `api.market.refresh` and observe it throws) but was not written since it is outside the harness's literal 7-claim list; flagging it here because it lives in the exact files under audit and was still reproducible on read.

subfindings.claim: Nested per-product reads across insights.ts dashboard queries
subfindings.evidence: convex/insights.ts: `activity` (104-240) does, per non-archived watch (up to MAX_WATCHES=40), a nested `watchChecks` query (116-120); per active purchase (up to MAX_PURCHASES=40), a nested `.collect()` of `items` by_purchase (134-137) and, per item, a nested `priceChecks` query (139-143); per claim (up to MAX_CLAIMS=40), three more nested `.collect()`s — `drafts` by_claim (195-199), `replies` by_claim (204-208), `ledgerEvents` by_claim (218-222). `sources` (267-357) repeats the same watch/purchase/item nesting plus a per-watch `offers` query (316-319). `priceHistory` (529-590) and `trackedTable` (593-628) nest a `confirmedOffers`+`storeSeries` call per watch, each of which itself queries `offerChecks` per confirmed offer (486-520, up to MAX_OFFER_STORES=8 per watch). priceWatch.ts `eligibleItems` (173-189) nests, per item scanned (up to SCAN_LIMIT=500 every 6h tick), a `db.get(purchase)` + `latestPolicy` query (up to 20 rows) + `hasOpenPriceClaim` `.collect()` (122-129, 149-167).
subfindings.repro: Read directly; no test needed to confirm the nesting exists (it is the literal control flow). Empirically exercised in a throwaway convex-test (real Convex transaction limits enabled via `transactionLimits: true`) seeding 40 purchases x 50 items x 12 priceChecks (26,040 documents, the code's own stated per-parent maximums): `api.insights.activity` completed in ~25s wall-clock under the fake backend without erroring — the nesting is real and costly, but the outer per-parent `.take()` caps (MAX_WATCHES/MAX_PURCHASES/MAX_CLAIMS=40, MAX_ITEMS_PER_PURCHASE=50) keep total reads (~26k) under convex-test's enforced 32,000 documentsRead ceiling in this specific worst case. Test file and temp vitest config were deleted after the run per instructions; repo `git status` is clean.

subfindings.claim: Serialized (non-parallel) fan-out over per-product reads
subfindings.evidence: Still sequential (a `for` loop awaiting inside the loop body, no `Promise.all`): convex/insights.ts `activity` (112, 124, 176, 195, 204, 218 — every per-watch/per-purchase/per-item/per-claim child read is awaited one at a time), `sources` (304, 335), `priceHistory`'s `offersByWatch` build (538: `for (const w of watches) offersByWatch.set(w._id, await confirmedOffers(...))`), `storeSeries`'s per-offer loop (506-518), and `priceWatch.ts` `eligibleItems` (180-186, sequential over up to 500 items) and `runAll`'s scheduling loop (482-486, sequential `scheduler.runAfter` calls — low-cost, but still not batched). By contrast, this WAS fixed in other read paths in the same review cycle: `watches.ts` `list` (270-274) uses `Promise.all` across the per-watch summarise calls, `watches.ts` `list`'s LIVE_STATUSES page fetch (256-264) uses `Promise.all`, `insights.ts`'s own `liveWatches` helper (443-451) uses `Promise.all` across the 3 status pages, and `offers.ts` `searchOffers`/`recheckConfirmedOffers` (477-486, 652-663) explicitly parallelize their per-page/per-offer scrapes with a comment citing exactly this rationale ("the reads are independent... run them together"). So the fix was applied inconsistently: offers.ts and watches.ts list-shaped reads got parallelized, insights.ts's own nested child reads and priceWatch.ts's eligibility scan did not.
subfindings.repro: Static: cite the `for` loops above versus the `Promise.all` call sites listed. Not a race condition (nothing here is a mutation or concurrency hazard) — it's a latency/throughput characteristic of a single query execution, so a convex-test race harness does not apply; the right test would be a wall-clock comparison (which I ran informally above: ~25s under the fake backend for the sequential `activity` path at 26k documents) rather than a pass/fail assertion.

subfindings.claim: Unbounded .collect() calls
subfindings.evidence: Two different situations exist under the same code pattern. (a) Transitively bounded despite no `.take()` on the read itself: `insights.ts:137` (`items` by_purchase) and `intake.ts:441` (`items` by_purchase) are `.collect()` with no limit, but every write path enforces MAX_ITEMS_PER_PURCHASE=50 (limits.ts:140) at insert time, so these can never exceed 50 rows; `claims.ts:52-55` and `intake.ts:486` `.collect()` claims by_item are naturally capped by `openClaim`'s own one-open-claim-per-(item,type) rule (claims.ts:56-66, D44). (b) Genuinely uncapped in both code and data model: `claims.ts:get` (353-399) `.collect()`s `ledgerEvents` (360-363), `drafts` (364-368), `replies` (369-372), `followUps` (373-376), and `claimNotes` (377-380) by_claim with no `.take()` anywhere and no write-time ceiling on total row count per claim over its lifetime (the only per-claim cap, MAX_SENDS_PER_CLAIM=3 in drafts.ts:456-457, bounds *sent* emails, not draft/reply/ledger/note row count); `insights.ts:198,207,221` repeat the same three unbounded `.collect()`s inside `activity`'s per-claim loop; `claims.ts:applyEvent` (204-208) `.collect()`s the full ledgerEvents history on every single ledger write (to recompute balance) with no cap. In practice growth is slow (daily budgets throttle draft/reply/retry creation), but the review's own framing ("establish maximum legitimate child counts") has not been done for any of these five relations — there is no constant, comment, or test asserting a ceiling.
subfindings.repro: Read the code; no test in the repo asserts a bound on these collections (grepped all *.test.ts — none references a per-claim draft/reply/ledgerEvent/followUp/claimNote count ceiling). subfindings.evidence: Under the code's own stated per-parent maximums (insights.ts MAX_WATCHES/MAX_PURCHASES/MAX_CLAIMS=40, limits.ts MAX_ITEMS_PER_PURCHASE=50, insights.ts CHECKS_PER_PRODUCT=12), `api.insights.activity` — the single heaviest read path in the app (three levels of nesting: watch/purchase -> item -> check, plus per-claim children) — does NOT trip Convex's real per-transaction limits.

Fixture 2: doubled to 80 purchases (same items/checks per purchase) to test whether growing a user's *total* data beyond the read-time cap changes anything — it did not error either, because `userPurchases`'s `.take(MAX_PURCHASES)` (insights.ts:94-101) bounds the outer scan via an index regardless of total row count, so purchases 41-80 are never touched by the query. Caveat: only `insights.activity` was empirically tested (it is the worst case among insights.ts's functions by nesting depth); `sources`, `priceHistory`, and `trackedTable` were reasoned analytically (smaller MAX constants: 30 watches, 100 offer-rows/watch via WATCH_ROWS, 120/20 chart points) but not run — I judge them lower-risk, not zero-risk. `priceWatch.eligibleItems`'s worst case (~500 items x ~3 nested reads, dominated by `latestPolicy`'s up-to-20-row scan) was reasoned to land near ~12,000 documentsRead, also under the cap, but likewise not empirically run. Note also that the REPO's OWN test suite (test.setup.ts:15, `convexTest(schema, modules)` with no `transactionLimits`) never enforces these limits at all, so none of the existing 575 tests could ever have caught a real transaction-limit failure even if one existed — that gap in the test harness is itself worth flagging separately from this specific claim's outcome.

subfindings.claim: No per-user fairness when global provider budgets are exhausted
subfindings.evidence: convex/watches.ts `sweep` (739-763): reads one global page (WATCH_SWEEP_PAGE=50) off `by_status_nextCheck` ascending across ALL users, then trims it to whatever `takeGlobalBudget` still allows (750-751) — no per-user slice or round-robin; a user whose watches happen to have the earliest `nextCheckAt` values can occupy the whole page on a given tick. convex/priceWatch.ts `eligibleItems`/`runAll` (173-189, 474-489): reads the newest SCAN_LIMIT=500 items table-wide (not per-user, no index on user), and `runAll` takes up to FANOUT_LIMIT=50 (via `takeGlobalPriceChecks`) from whichever items happened to survive the sequential eligibility scan first — again no per-user cap. convex/intake.ts `retryFailed` (766-834): reads the oldest RETRY_PAGE=50 `failed` rows off `by_status` GLOBALLY (784-787), with no per-user fairness; the repo's own test "dead rows do not block newer failures behind them (H4)" (intake.test.ts:673-688) proves the mechanism directly — it seeds 50 unrunnable rows from ONE user and shows a later row (even from the same user) must wait a full extra tick, which is exactly the cross-user starvation shape (a noisy user's 50 dead/failed rows would identically delay a different user's single failed row by a tick) — the test just never varies `userId` to say so explicitly.
subfindings.repro: Static, and the H4 test above is a live demonstration of the underlying mechanism (single-user framing, same fairness mechanism). Not a race condition — deterministic ordering by index — so no convex-test fault injection is needed beyond what already exists; a direct reproduction would be a 2-user variant of the same H4 test asserting user B's failed row is delayed by user A's backlog, which does not currently exist anywhere in the suite (grepped priceWatch.test.ts, watches.test.ts, intake.test.ts for multi-user + volume combinations — none found).

subfindings.evidence: convex/schema.ts (33-199): no table (`watchChecks`, `priceChecks`, `offerChecks`, `marketPrices`, `mailLog`, `processedEvents`, `usage`, `claimNotes`) has a TTL/expiry field or any schema-level retention marker. convex/crons.ts (full file, 29 lines) registers exactly 3 jobs — `priceWatch.runAll`, `watches.sweep`, `intake.retryFailed` — none of which deletes or archives anything. `processedEvents.payload` (schema.ts:191-198) stores the full raw email (`intake.ts:838` notes it can be "up to 60 KB a row") indefinitely; there is no job that ever clears it even after the row reaches a terminal `succeeded`/`failed` state. repro:P06.title: Time and freshness correctness — watches.list/get (and offers.listForWatch) Date.now()-in-query claims

subfindings.claim: Foundational premise: watches.list/get bake Date.now() into reactive query summaries
subfindings.evidence: convex/watches.ts:269 (`list`: `const now = Date.now();`) and convex/watches.ts:289 (`get`: `summarise(watch, checks, Date.now(), ...)`) both snapshot the wall clock inside a Convex query handler. The project's own generated Convex guidelines explicitly warn against this: convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md ('Query guidelines') states 'Do not read the wall clock inside a query... results derived from Date.now()... can become stale, and wall-clock reads also reduce query-cache reuse... pass the current time in as an argument and let the client refresh it.' `now` is then threaded into `summarise()` (watches.ts:169-245): into `checking` (line ~209-212) and into `verdict()` (lib/verdict.ts:120-190, via the `now` field).
subfindings.repro: Static read of convex/watches.ts:248-303. No test exercises the live-subscription behavior; see notes on why convex-test cannot demonstrate the consequence directly.

subfindings.claim: Countdowns (next-check timer, 'last checked X ago') go stale in an open tab
subfindings.evidence: `nextCheckAt` and `lastCheckedAt` are returned as raw epoch-ms fields (watches.ts:87-88, 203-204), never pre-formatted with `now` baked in. The frontend recomputes the display text itself using a client-side ticking clock: src/lib/ui.ts:110-118 `useNow(everyMs=60_000)` (setInterval + setState), consumed by src/pages/Watching.tsx:216 and passed into src/components/watching/WatchCard.tsx:315,445-447 (`ago(now, watch.lastCheckedAt)`, `remainingLabel(watch.nextCheckAt - now)`) and src/components/watching/StoreCompare.tsx:94,283. Because these are pure functions of two raw numbers (one from the query, one from the 60s client tick), the visible countdown/elapsed text keeps updating correctly without needing the Convex subscription to re-push a new query result. This specific symptom does not reproduce on current code.
subfindings.repro: Code reading only: src/lib/ui.ts useNow + src/components/watching/time.ts `ago()` + WatchCard.tsx usage. No convex-test needed since this is a pure client-formatting path, not a query-output correctness question.

subfindings.claim: Search leases (offer-search cooldown/pending state) go stale in an open tab
subfindings.evidence: convex/offers.ts `listForWatch` (a query) snapshots `const now = Date.now()` at offers.ts:358 and derives two booleans/gates from it at write time: `searching` (offers.ts:396-397) and `nextFindAt` which is deliberately nulled out once expired (offers.ts:398: `nextFindAt !== null && nextFindAt > now ? nextFindAt : null`). The frontend gates the actual 'Search other stores' button strictly on this server-baked value, not on a client recompute: src/components/watching/StoreCompare.tsx:176 `canFind = watching && data !== undefined && !data.searching && data.nextFindAt === null`. The adjacent countdown TEXT does self-update via the client's `useNow()` tick (StoreCompare.tsx:183 `Search again in ${remainingLabel(data.nextFindAt - now)}`), but `remainingLabel` floors negative durations to '0m' (src/lib/ui.ts: `Math.max(0, Math.floor(ms/60_000))`). So once the cooldown genuinely expires in wall-clock time with no other write to that watch's offers, an open tab is left showing the self-contradictory state 'Search again in 0m' next to a permanently-disabled button, until some unrelated write to that watch retriggers the subscription. The mutation itself (`find`, offers.ts:268-296) independently recomputes eligibility with a fresh `Date.now()` in `consumeFindLimit` (offers.ts:241-266), so this is a UI-only staleness bug, not an authorization gap.
subfindings.repro: convex/offers.test.ts:337-360 ('schedules one search, reports searching, and enforces the per-watch cooldown') only ever calls `listForWatch` at explicitly chosen system times (fresh evaluations each time) — it never asserts what a single already-open subscription would show across a time advance with zero writes, so it doesn't catch this. This is a live-reactivity fault, not a pure data-state bug: convex-test's `t.query()` (see node_modules/convex-test/dist/index.d.ts) has no `.watch()`/subscribe API — every call is a brand-new evaluation, so it cannot show whether an already-subscribed real client is ever pushed the corrected value absent a write. Demonstrating it needs a live `ConvexReactClient`/`useQuery` integration or browser test against a running deployment (advance real wall-clock time, perform no writes, assert whether the subscription callback fires) — out of scope here (task disallows `npx convex dev`) and overlaps P10's planned browser suite.

subfindings.claim: Cooldowns (watch 'Check now' cooldown / checking indicator) go stale in an open tab
subfindings.evidence: The mutation-side eligibility check IS fresh and authoritative and does not have this problem: `checkNow` (watches.ts:380-400) and `find` (offers.ts:268-296/241-266) both recompute cooldown against a freshly-read `Date.now()` at mutation time, independent of any stale query value — clicking 'Check now' after the real cooldown has elapsed always succeeds even if the UI still showed it disabled. The UI-facing gate is the part that can go stale: `checking` (watches.ts:209-212, inside `summarise`) is `checkRequestedAt > (lastCheckedAt ?? 0) && now - checkRequestedAt < WATCH_CHECK_COOLDOWN_MS` baked from `Date.now()` at query-eval time, and the 'Check now' button is disabled purely on it: src/components/watching/WatchCard.tsx:459 `disabled={busy || watch.checking}` (no client-side recompute). In the common path this self-heals fast because `recordWatchCheck` (watches.ts:634-727) unconditionally patches `lastCheckedAt` on completion (line ~688), and that write retriggers any open subscription for real — so ordinary checks do not exhibit staleness. The gap is a fault window: in `checkWatch` (watches.ts:593-626) only the `observePrice` call is wrapped in try/catch (lines 601-606); the following `ctx.runMutation(internal.watches.recordWatchCheck, ...)` call (line 607) is unguarded, so if it throws (e.g. transient error, or the watch was concurrently deleted), the watch document never changes again and an already-open subscription's cached `checking:true` (and the disabled 'Checking…' button) has nothing to retrigger it — it would stay stuck past WATCH_CHECK_COOLDOWN_MS (600,000 ms, convex/limits.ts:18) until an unrelated write to that watch happens or the client reconnects/refreshes.
subfindings.repro: Wrote and ran a throwaway convex-test (temp file + temp vitest config under /private/tmp, deleted after use) that: (1) seeds `checkRequestedAt` with no completing write, confirms `get().watch.checking === true`; (2) advances fake system time past WATCH_CHECK_COOLDOWN_MS with zero writes, re-calls `get()`, and confirms it now correctly returns `checking:false`. This proves the computation is a pure, uncached function of `Date.now()` at call time (no stored 'expired' flag) — the mechanism is correct IF re-evaluated. It cannot go further: convex-test has no subscription/watch API, so it cannot show whether a real, already-open browser tab (that received `checking:true` before the time advance) would ever be pushed that corrected `false` value absent an intervening write — per the Convex guidelines doc, it would not, since 'queries are not rerun merely because time advances.' Verifying that needs a live reactive-client/browser test, not run here.

subfindings.claim: Verdict age (how stale is the price behind the verdict) goes stale/blind in an open tab
subfindings.evidence: The root cause here is not really query-caching but a data-modeling gap: `verdict()` (convex/lib/verdict.ts:120-190) only uses its `now` argument to filter out future-dated observations (line 128: `h.observedAt <= now`); `spanMs` (line 130) is computed purely from historical `observedAt` values, never from `now - lastObservedAt`. So nothing in the verdict computation measures or reports how long ago `currentCents` was actually confirmed — the label/reason text (e.g. '$46.00 is the lowest price we have seen since Sep 20, 2026') is byte-identical whether the underlying acceptance happened a minute ago or 60+ days ago, as long as no newer accepted observation has displaced it.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway convex-test (same file as above, deleted after use): seeded 3 accepted prices spanning 8 days (clearing MIN_OBSERVATIONS/MIN_SPAN_DAYS), captured the verdict, then advanced 60 days and recorded one FAILED check (no new price). Re-fetched `watches.get`: `verdict.label` and `verdict.reason` were byte-identical to the fresh read from 60 days earlier, with no qualifier about the price's age. Existing coverage in convex/lib/verdict.test.ts (e.g. 'ignores observations dated in the future') tests the future-date filter but has no case pairing an old `currentCents` with a much-later `now`.

subfindings.claim: Stale last-known prices are shown without qualification
subfindings.evidence: `watch.lastCents` (convex/schema.ts:84-92) is set once on acceptance (watches.ts recordWatchCheck, `patch.lastCents = observedCents` only when `observedCents !== undefined`) and is never cleared, decayed, or flagged by any number of subsequent failed checks. `watchSummary.lastCents` (watches.ts:90) is returned unconditionally as `currentCents` (watches.ts:180,205) and drives both the headline price and the verdict (finding above), with no accompanying 'as of' timestamp distinct from the misleading `lastCheckedAt` (see next finding).
subfindings.repro: Same throwaway test as the 'verdict age' finding: `staleRead.watch.lastCents === 4_600` (the price from day 8) is unchanged and unqualified after a 60-day-later failed check on day 68.

subfindings.claim: Last successful observation is not shown separately from last attempt
subfindings.evidence: `watchSummary` (watches.ts:76-128) has exactly one 'when' field for check activity, `lastCheckedAt`, and `recordWatchCheck` (watches.ts:687-689) stamps it to `now` unconditionally on every check, accepted or rejected/failed alike (`patch.lastCheckedAt = now` is not gated on `observedCents !== undefined`; only `patch.lastCents` is). There is no `lastObservedAt`/`lastPriceAt`/'price confirmed at' field anywhere in `watchSummary`. The only place the true last-accepted timestamp survives is buried inside the `spark` array (watches.ts:216-219, truncated to at most 30 accepted points and itself evicted once VERDICT_WINDOW=60 consecutive checks pass without an acceptance) — none of the consuming UI (WatchCard.tsx 'Last checked' line 445, PriceHistoryCard.tsx:108, SourcesCard.tsx:65) reads `spark` for freshness; they all read `lastCheckedAt` directly. The identical pattern repeats in offers.ts: `priceFields()` (offers.ts:183-200) sets `lastCheckedAt: now` unconditionally regardless of `accepted`, so an offer's 'last checked' is likewise attempt-time, not success-time.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway convex-test: after the day-68 failed check, `staleRead.watch.lastCheckedAt === failedAt` (day 68) while the last accepted spark point's `observedAt === lastGoodAt` (day 8) — a 60-day gap the API surfaces nowhere as a distinct field. Confirmed `Object.keys(staleRead.watch)` contains neither `lastObservedAt` nor `lastPriceAt`.

subfindings.claim: Failed reads make old data look fresh (the P06 acceptance criterion: 'days of failed reads cannot show an unqualified fresh good price')
subfindings.evidence: Direct consequence of the three findings above: `lastCheckedAt` is bumped by a failed check (looks fresh), `lastCents`/verdict are unchanged (are actually stale), and nothing in the returned shape or the primary UI line reconciles the two. The one existing mitigation, `lastNote` (watches.ts:213, rendered at WatchCard.tsx:452 as '· No price last time: <note>'), only ever reflects the SINGLE most-recent check's failure text — it says a read failed, but never says how old the displayed price actually is, and disappears the moment any later check (even another failure with a different/no note) occurs.
subfindings.repro: Throwaway convex-test 'shows a confident, present-tense verdict off a 60-day-old accepted price after a failed re-check...' (temp file under /private/tmp, run via `npx vitest run --config <temp config rooted at the repo>`, both assertions passed, file deleted afterward). It asserts the fresh-vs-stale verdict label/reason are identical and that the reason text contains no age-qualifying language (`not.toMatch(/day|week|month|old|stale|ago/i)`) even though the last acceptance is 60 days behind the (recent, failed) `lastCheckedAt`.

existing_tests: convex/watches.test.ts: creation seeds `checking:true` right after `create` (line ~147) but never tests it flipping to false via re-query vs. via a real completing write, and never tests a long-gap-then-failure verdict scenario.

convex/watches.test.ts describe('watches.checkNow cooldown') (~line 292-330): tests the mutation-side cooldown boundary (T0+COOLDOWN-1 rejected, T0+COOLDOWN allowed) — confirms the AUTHORITATIVE mutation path is fresh/correct, but does not touch the query-side `checking` display flag's own staleness.

subfindings.claim: Possible foreign-ID acceptance on public ACTIONS (drafts.generate, intake.paste, policies.refresh, profiles.ensureInbox) and on mutations taking a second document id (e.g. purchases.confirm's item ids).
